NENEMI.
Come back.

Nenemi — Nahuatl for to return, to come back. A calm home for ADHD brains: somewhere to set things down and pick them back up, without ever losing your place. This book keeps everything true to that — and to the people it's for.

01 — Story & purpose

Why NENEMI exists

Read this first. If a design or word choice ever feels off, it's because it broke something here.

Most productivity apps are built for brains that don't work like ours — and they punish the way ADHD actually works. Streaks you break. Tasks that turn red. A quiet voice that says you're behind, again. NENEMI is built on the opposite promise.

Here's the ADHD day we design for: you start something, then hit a wall, get pulled away, or your attention just goes. You walk away mid-thought — not because you failed, but because that's how the brain works. Later you come back, and normally you'd have to rebuild everything from nothing. That friction is exactly what makes ADHD folks abandon an app for good.

With NENEMI, you come back and it's exactly where you left it. Your place is kept. Nothing lost, nothing scolding you, no starting over. That's the whole product, and the whole name: nenemi, to come back. We built the app around returning because returning is the single hardest — and most important — thing an ADHD brain has to do.

The mark is a place, not a task.

A task list says "you owe this, you're behind." A place says "your stuff is safe here — come back when you can." Our N is a place: a stepped path you climb, leave, and return to.

Its terraced steps nod to the Aztec xicalcoliuhqui — the stepped-fret carved into pyramids at Teotihuacan and Templo Mayor. Stone terraces don't move: you climb them, you leave, they stay exactly as they were, and you return.

What we believe about ADHD

You're not behind — you're mid-process. ADHD isn't a discipline problem or a character flaw. It's a different relationship with attention, memory, and time. Walking away isn't failing; it's Tuesday. So we never treat a pause as a lapse to correct. The skill that actually helps isn't "focus harder" — it's returning without friction, and that's what NENEMI makes effortless. Made for your brain. Not their expectations.

02 — Logo

The mark & lockups

The shape is locked. Use these files exactly so people learn it as ours.

A single stepped N — the built place you come back to. Solid, calm, and confident: terraced steps on one leg, a smooth diagonal with a soft rounded foot, and a quiet notch up top. Always solid ink, warm-white, teal, or maíz — never outlined, never gradient.

Wordmark

Set in a heavy geometric face, spaced caps: NENEMI. Bold and even, never condensed or lightweight, never all-teal on white.

Clear space & minimum size

Keep clear space of one step (one terrace of the mark) on all sides. Minimum symbol size 20px — it still reads as the mark at favicon scale.

03 — Color

Palette

Protect ADHD attention. A busy, loud screen is a sensory tax — every extra hue pulls focus. So we stay quiet on purpose.

Light and warm, ink for the work, one calm slate-teal as the signal, and maíz for warmth and small wins. The teal went deeper and calmer than the old bright cyan — more grown-up, easier to live with all day.

App Ground#F5F6F5Default background. Soft, never stark white.
Paper#FAF8F3Warm editorial surfaces & covers.
Ink#111312Type, the mark, primary buttons.
Signature Teal#3C8692The calm signal — here / now / open.
Teal Deep#2C6670Teal text on light, pressed states.
Maíz#E9BE55Warmth & wins. Roots. Use sparingly.
Maíz Deep#B98F2AMaíz as text on light.
Dim#63696ASecondary copy, meta.
Line#E5E7E6Hairline borders & dividers.

The meaning & the ratio

Teal = tended (here, now, your place is kept). Maíz = warmth & return (a small win, welcome back). In Mesoamerican myth, humans are made from maize — so teal + maíz is tended + rooted. Ratio: mostly paper + ink, teal as the quiet signal, maíz only for warmth. Never teal and maíz fighting on the same element.

04 — Typography

Type system

Confident headlines, plain calm body. Easy to scan — which matters when reading takes effort.

Aa
Archivo Black
Display · Wordmark
Headlines, screen titles, the wordmark. Heavy, geometric, sure of itself.
Aa
System Sans
Body · UI
Helvetica / SF / system. Body, labels, buttons. Neutral and clear.
Aa
Monospace
Meta · Status
Timestamps, counts, section numbers. Quiet and technical.

Rules

Display for titles and moments, never paragraphs. Body stays ink or Dim — never teal. The wordmark is always the heavy geometric face at even spacing.

05 — Spacing & shape

Space, radius, elevation

Lots of breathing room. Crowded screens overwhelm ADHD brains — when in doubt, add space.

4 · xsicon gaps, tight inset
8 · smlabel-to-value, chips
16 · mdcard padding, list gaps
24 · lgcard interior, blocks
40 · xlbetween components
82 · 2xlsection rhythm

Radius & elevation

Cards & rooms 18–22px · buttons & pills 100px · inputs 14px. One soft shadow lifts cards off the ground; dividers and chips stay flat. Calm, never flashy.

Room card

Motion

Everything reads as returning, not loading. Slow, eased transitions (400–700ms). Nothing bounces or flashes — sudden motion hijacks an ADHD brain. A calm room you re-enter, not a slot machine.

07 — In the product

How the brand behaves

This is the brand doing its job — helping an ADHD brain come back and re-enter without friction.

Coming back is the hard part, so every room answers the two questions that get you moving again: Where did I leave off? and What's the next small thing? Everything else waits quietly below.

Where you left off
Where you left off
You were listing who you've chatted with.

Your own closing note, shown back verbatim. If missing, AI writes it — so "left off" is always true.

What's next
Say one messy thought on Home.
Start
Too big? Make it smaller.

ADHD paralysis comes from tasks that feel too big. One next move, always reducible.

"I'm stuck"
I'm stuck

Getting stuck is expected, not a failure. A permanent button, always one tap away.

Warm wins
"You came back."
"3 days in a row."

Maíz celebrates returning, never completing. Warmth, never pressure.

08 — Voice & tone

How NENEMI speaks

The words matter most. ADHD folks have heard "you're not trying hard enough" their whole lives — one wrong nag and we become one more voice that let them down.

Warm, plain, human. NENEMI never shames, never nags, never optimizes. We are relentlessly on your side, then get out of the way.

We say

"You didn't fall behind. You stepped away."

"Welcome back. You left off here."

"Whatever's in your head, put it here."

"Pick up exactly where you left off."

"Too big? Make it smaller."

"Come back anytime."

We don't say

"You're behind." / streak broken

"3 tasks overdue!"

"Boost your productivity."

"Don't forget!" (urgency, alarm)

Clinical / "ADHD tool" framing

Anything that counts down or scolds

Principles

Plain over clever · Reassuring over motivating · Present, not pushy. The win we deliver is "oh — I know exactly where I was," not "I finished everything." We measure success by whether someone came back. Built by a neurodivergent founder, for neurodivergent minds — ADHD is the entire reason NENEMI exists.

09 — How we know

We did the work. We're not done.

This is why we get to make an ADHD app. Not a hunch — literature, professionals, and the community that lived it.

Every decision in this book traces back to four things we keep coming back to — and we're never finished learning.

01

The literature

We read the clinical and academic research on ADHD — attention, working memory, time — and design against it, not around it.

02

The professionals

We've met with clinicians and specialists who work with ADHD every day, and pressure-tested the product against what they see.

03

The community

We talk with people living with ADHD — their real days, their real friction. They shaped where NENEMI is, and keep shaping it.

04

Lived experience

Built by a neurodivergent founder. Not ADHD studied from outside — understood from the inside.

ADHD has a long, real history — we honor it

Early 1900s
First clinical descriptions
Physicians begin documenting the pattern of inattention and impulsivity we now call ADHD.
Mid–late 1900s
Named, renamed, refined
Formally recognized and reframed as understanding deepens — toward today's fuller picture of attention regulation.
Today
A living, evolving science
Research keeps growing — executive function, emotional regulation, how ADHD shows up across every kind of person.
Every day, ongoing
NENEMI keeps learning
As the science evolves and the community tells us more, so does NENEMI. "We're never finished learning" is a promise.
Our standard: we only ever claim what's true. No invented statistics, no borrowed authority — real reading, real conversations, real experience. That honesty is part of never letting our people down.

From the founder

Marcos's photo
goes here

I built NENEMI because I needed it. My brain doesn't run in straight lines — I start things, get pulled away, and come back to find I've lost the thread completely. For years I blamed myself for that. Every app I tried just made it worse: another list turning red, another streak I broke, another quiet reminder that I was behind.

So I made the thing I wished existed — a place that simply keeps my spot while I'm gone, and welcomes me back without judgment. I talked to clinicians, I talked to other people living with ADHD, I read everything I could, and I kept checking it against my own experience. NENEMI is the result, and it's still learning.

If your brain works like mine: you're not broken, and you're not behind. You just needed somewhere to come back to. Welcome home.

Marcos
Founder, NENEMI
